findings.text: Global dispatch pointer mce_threshold_vector initially refers to default_threshold_interrupt and is invoked on each threshold event by sysvec_threshold. Implementations may replace the pointer to provide platform handling while preserving indirect dispatch.

System vector entry sysvec_threshold handles threshold interrupts by performing entry tracing then accounting then indirect dispatch through mce_threshold_vector then exit tracing then APIC end of interrupt. It always ends with end of interrupt signaling.

Per processor storage storm_desc provides one mca_storm_desc instance on each processor for threshold storm tracking. Type details live elsewhere while allocation discipline is strictly per processor.

Structure ucode_patch links cached images through plist and carries data pointer plus size plus patch_id plus equiv_cpu. The list node allows global cache membership while remaining fields identify image bytes and target processor equivalence.

Framing constants are magic 0x00414d44 for containers and type 0x00000000 for equivalence tables and type 0x00000001 for patch sections and 12 bytes container header length and 8 bytes section header length. They discriminate valid data and locate length fields.

Packed structure equiv_cpu_entry holds installed_cpu plus fixed_errata_mask plus fixed_errata_compare plus equiv_cpu plus res. No padding is present so table byte length divided by entry size yields entry count.

Packed header microcode_header_amd starts with data_code and patch_id for identity. It then carries data description fields mc_patch_data_id with length mc_patch_data_len and flag init_flag plus checksum mc_patch_data_checksum. Device fields nb_dev_id and sb_dev_id must be zero for support. Revision fields processor_rev_id with nb_rev_id and sb_rev_id plus interface bios_api_rev follow ending with reserved1 and match_reg array.

Patch image microcode_amd consists of header hdr followed by variable length payload mpb. Callers address the header data marker field when requesting load and treat remaining words as microcode payload.
Scan result descriptor cont_desc holds selected patch pointer mc plus size psize plus container start data plus extent size. It reports the chosen image and its enclosing container span.
In memory equivalence table equiv_table is represented by count num_entries plus pointer entry to packed entries. Modern processors bypass this table entirely.

Two overlay views translate between CPUID leaf one EAX and microcode revision encodings. One view zen_patch_rev splits revision into revision byte of eight bits plus stepping of four bits plus model of four bits plus reserved of four bits plus extended model of four bits plus extended family of eight bits and also as full word ucode_rev. The other view cpuid_1_eax splits CPUID value into stepping of four bits plus model of four bits plus family of four bits plus reserved of four bits plus extended model of four bits plus extended family of eight bits plus reserved of four bits and also as full word full.
Authenticity record patch_digest pairs identifier patch_id with digest sha256. Lookup is ordered by identifier to support binary search.

Boot processor CPUID leaf one EAX is captured once during early load in bsp_cpuid_1_eax and thereafter treated as read only. Global boolean sha_check enables digest verification by default and can be cleared once via command line option microcode dot amd_sha_check with value off an action that also marks the kernel as out of specification.

Diagnostic messages from this component carry microcode prefix defined by pr_fmt. Debug messages via ucode_dbg are emitted only when debug configuration is enabled otherwise they vanish. Early initrd lookup uses fixed firmware path kernel slash x86 slash microcode slash AuthenticAMD dot bin.

Conversion cpuid_to_ucode_rev copies stepping plus model plus extended model plus extended family from CPUID view into revision view while discarding family. Reverse conversion ucode_rev_to_cpuid copies stepping plus model plus extended model plus extended family back and forces family to 0xf and clears reserved bits allowing modern patch identity comparison without equivalence table.

Revision cutoff mapping keyed by revision shifted right eight bits uses pairs high to cutoff as follows 0x80012 to 0x8001277 then 0x80082 to 0x800820f then 0x83010 to 0x830107c then 0x86001 to 0x860010e then 0x86081 to 0x8608108 then 0x87010 to 0x8701034 then 0x8a000 to 0x8a0000a then 0xa0010 to 0xa00107a then 0xa0011 to 0xa0011da then 0xa0012 to 0xa001243 then 0xa0082 to 0xa00820e then 0xa1011 to 0xa101153 then 0xa1012 to 0xa10124e then 0xa1081 to 0xa108109 then 0xa2010 to 0xa20102f then 0xa2012 to 0xa201212 then 0xa4041 to 0xa404109 then 0xa5000 to 0xa500013 then 0xa6012 to 0xa60120a then 0xa7041 to 0xa704109 then 0xa7052 to 0xa705208 then 0xa7080 to 0xa708009 then 0xa70c0 to 0xa70c009 then 0xaa001 to 0xaa00116 then 0xaa002 to 0xaa00218 then 0xb0021 to 0xb002146 then 0xb0081 to 0xb008111 then 0xb1010 to 0xb101046 then 0xb2040 to 0xb204031 then 0xb4040 to 0xb404031 then 0xb4041 to 0xb404101 then 0xb6000 to 0xb600031 then 0xb6080 to 0xb608031 then 0xb7000 to 0xb700031. Other keys yield zero.

Digest enforcement applies only on processors with entry signing namely families 0x17 and 0x19 always and family 0x1a for model ranges up to 0x2f and 0x40 to 0x4f and 0x60 to 0x7f. When a cutoff exists digests are required only if current revision does not exceed the cutoff otherwise verification is required and unknown revisions emit diagnostic requesting report.

Patch authentication via verify_sha256_digest first bypasses when signing is absent or not required or globally disabled then searches sorted digest table phashes by patch identifier via cmp_id and bsearch and fails if no entry exists then hashes supplied bytes via sha256 and fails on mismatch while dumping computed digest otherwise succeeds.

Current revision via get_patch_level is obtained from patch level register except under debug on hypervisors where per processor cache microcode_rev with boot derived base_rev is used. Zero hardware reading on older families is returned as zero while on modern families it is synthesized from boot CPUID with one time notice.

Equivalence lookup via find_equiv_id returns zero immediately on modern families or when table is missing or empty otherwise it scans linearly for installed signature match and returns associated equivalent identifier or zero when no entry matches.

Container acceptance via verify_container requires length beyond container header and correct magic. Equivalence acceptance via verify_equivalence_table additionally requires modern family bypass or correct table type plus table length holding at least one entry and fitting within remaining buffer.

Patch section acceptance via __verify_patch_section requires at least section header plus correct patch type plus declared size covering at least header reporting declared size outward. Size acceptance via __verify_patch_size on family 0x15 and newer only checks fit in buffer while older families enforce per family maxima and reject unknown families.
Legacy patch payload maxima are 2048 bytes for families 0x10 through 0x12 and 1824 bytes for family 0x14. Newer families have no fixed maximum beyond container fit.

Patch validation via verify_patch yields three outcomes. Negative means malformed or unsupported and aborts container scan. Positive means well formed but not for this processor and skips to next patch. Zero means candidate for this processor. Unsupported chipset identifiers plus family mismatch derived from processor revision plus cutoff side mismatch all produce skip while truncation and size violations produce abort.

Candidate matching via mc_patch_matches on modern families compares full CPUID derived from patch identifier against boot CPUID while on older families it compares container equivalence identifier against patch processor revision field.

Container parsing via parse_container first validates framing and locates equivalence identifier then iterates over patch sections advancing by declared size plus header. It records last matching candidate and aborts iteration on malformed sections and returns zero when candidate was found with descriptor pointing at container extent otherwise returns bytes consumed so outer scanner scan_containers can advance to next container while guarding against size wraparound.

Application via __apply_microcode_amd first authenticates image over declared length then requests load through loader register using header marker address. On family 0x17 it invalidates translation for image start and for end when crossing page boundary then updates debug cache under hypervisors then rereads current level and reports success only when reread level equals patch identifier.

Early blobs prefer built in firmware via get_builtin_microcode using family specific name for family 0x15 and newer and generic name otherwise unavailable on thirty two bit builds falling back to initrd lookup at fixed Authentic AMD path via find_blobs_in_containers. Initrd location via find_microcode_in_initrd derives from boot parameters with sixty four bit extension handling and page offset adjustment overridden by relocated initrd start when present and empty when initrd support is disabled.

Early boot entry load_ucode_amd_bsp captures CPUID and records old revision and ensures processor signature state and scans containers for matching patch and applies it when stored revision is not newer recording new revision on success. It also honors command line switch to disable digest checking.
Runtime reload entry reload_ucode_amd looks up cached patch for given processor and applies it only when current revision is older emitting one time notice on success.
Application processor early entry load_ucode_amd_ap records processor signature for calling processor and invokes standard apply path for that processor.

Initrd lookup helper find_microcode_in_initrd resolves configured ramdisk extent and searches it as compressed archive data for caller supplied path returning empty data when initrd support is absent.

Cache identity via patch_cpus_equivalent on modern families compares full CPUID values derived from patch identifiers optionally ignoring stepping while older families compare equivalence identifiers. Newness via patch_newer on modern families rejects differing steppings and otherwise compares revision bytes while older families compare numeric patch identifiers.

Cache lookup via cache_find_patch builds probe from current revision and equivalence value and returns first equivalent entry. Insertion via update_cache replaces equivalent entry only when newcomer is newer and discards duplicates and skips incompatible steppings and otherwise appends. Clearing via free_cache unlinks every entry and releases both image and node storage.

Per processor apply via apply_microcode_amd first requires execution on target processor and cached patch reporting UCODE_NFOUND when absent. When current revision exceeds cached identifier it reports UCODE_OK without load otherwise it attempts load and reports UCODE_ERROR on failure or UCODE_UPDATED on success while refreshing per processor and global revision state including boot processor data when applicable. Collection via collect_cpu_info_amd captures signature and revision and links early loaded images for resume.

Risks include truncated container and section headers plus oversized legacy patches plus chipset specific images that are rejected plus digest mismatch or missing digest entries plus disabled digest verification that taints kernel plus page crossing images requiring extra invalidation plus container size wraparound plus applying older revisions over newer ones which callers must avoid by revision comparison.
Unexpected threshold interrupt signals that dispatch pointer was never customized for platform so default handler only logs vector number and returns without corrective action.
